title: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Step through training data, training, and new data for a spam classifier and a customer clustering model side by side, and compare what each kind of learning is given, what it learns, and what it outputs.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to compare supervised and unsupervised learning by explaining what data each one is given, what it learns, and what kind of output it produces.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side step-through of two worked examples with a comparison table
keyQuestions: What does the supervised learner have that the unsupervised learner does not?
Why can K-Means report "Group B" but not "frequent shopper"?
If the labels were erased from the emails, what could a model still learn from them?
commonMisconceptions: Unsupervised learning predicts labels (it only finds structure such as groups; people decide what the groups mean).
Supervised learning means a person watches the model while it trains (the supervision is the labeled answers in the training data).
The colors in the clustering plot are labels that came with the data (the algorithm assigns them after training).
A clustering result can be scored for accuracy the way a classifier is (there are no correct answers to compare against).
assessmentOpportunities: Given a short description of a data set and a goal, students state whether the task is supervised or unsupervised, name what plays the role of X and (if present) y, and describe the form of the model's output.
